- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), as models tend to underreact to bearish signals.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.30) — models often overreact to bullish sentiment, leading to lagged or delayed price spikes.
- When sentiment turns sharply negative, model forecasts often overshoot the true price by 2–5% in the first 5–7 days; apply a 1–2% downward correction.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- Lagged spikes: if true price spikes > 5% above 10-day moving average, model often lags by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to anticipate 1–2 days ahead.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term (1–3 day) forecasts when sentiment is volatile — reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% if sentiment swings > 0.50 in 3 consecutive days.
